annotations.annotation_text: Page 39 opens Book 1, Chapter 2 ("The Encounter in Phoenix Park") during the Age of Gods phase. This passage continues HCE's mysterious sin in Phoenix Park, the spread of gossip through Dublin, and the Cad with the pipe, featuring HCE, the Cad, Hosty. The nocturnal dream-narrative layers Dublin topography, world mythology, and linguistic alchemy into polysemic prose.

annotations.annotation_text: Issy/daughter figure "maggies" on page 39 ("The Encounter in Phoenix Park"): the narcissistic mirror-daughter, modeled on Isolde and Swift's dual muses Stella and Vanessa, appears here within HCE's mysterious sin in Phoenix Park, the spread of gossip through Dublin, and the Cad with the pipe. Her prismatic splitting into twenty-eight Rainbow Girls reflects the cycle's Age of Gods phase through youthful seduction and self-reflection.

annotations.annotation_text: Mid-page polysemic node on page 39 ("The Encounter in Phoenix Park"): Joyce weaves multilingual puns across 60+ languages — etymological roots from the Contemporary Literature Press lexicons (Romanian, Scandinavian, Slavic, Classical) intersect with local Dublin speech rhythms. The Age of Gods dream-logic transforms ordinary syntax into a palimpsest of global literary and mythic references.
